text: Silence does not "settle". Words do not "hang in the air". Knowledge does not "sit in the room". History does not "press". A truth does not "land".
Silence doesn't "settle"; it waits for the reader to mistake vagueness for depth.
Words do not hang in the air; they supposedly circle the room until someone confesses.
Knowledge does not sit in the room. It watches from the corner like a verdict.
History does not press. Memory does not hold. The paragraph calls that insight.
A truth does not land because landing would make it too ordinary.
Grief does not "arrive". Love does not "breathe". Both lines posture as revelation.
Time never waits. Absence never sleeps. The cadence performs depth without adding a claim.
Belonging cannot "bloom". Certainty cannot "hold". The negatives do the decoration.
The old wound does not whisper; the sentence only borrows pressure from metaphor.
Our shared silence will not "open" no matter how long the paragraph stares at it.
Meaning would not "carry" us; it would stand nearby and refuse the obvious verb.
The paint does not settle evenly in cold rooms, so the second coat needs more time.
The invoice does not land until Friday because the vendor batch runs overnight.
The team waited in silence while the room settled after the announcement.
Use `Silence does not "settle".` as a bad example in the guide, then explain the rule plainly.

Outside the code block, the document describes the fixture format.
The words on the sign do not hang from wires; each letter is painted directly on metal.
Truths don't "land" in this passage; they drift until the ending pretends to resolve them.
Desire did not "burn". Fear did not "move". Doubt did not "speak".
